# Renal Cryoablation — Authorization Guide

Subtitle: CPT Codes · ICD-10 · Payer Requirements

backHref: /renal-cryoablation

## CPT Codes

| CPT Code | Description | Guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50593 | Ablation, renal tumor(s), unilateral, percutaneous, cryotherapy | CT or US |
| 76940 | Ultrasound guidance for, and monitoring of, parenchymal tissue ablation (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure) | US add-on |
| 77013 | Computed tomography guidance for, and monitoring of, parenchymal tissue ablation (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure) | CT add-on |
| 77022 | Magnetic resonance imaging guidance for, and monitoring of, parenchymal tissue ablation (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure) | MRI add-on |
| 50200 | Renal biopsy; percutaneous, by trocar or needle | Pre-procedure biopsy |
| 74178 | CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast (pre-procedure planning) | Diagnostic |
| 74183 | MRI abdomen with and without contrast (pre-procedure planning) | Diagnostic |

Note: CPT 50593 is the primary code for percutaneous renal cryoablation. Always append the appropriate imaging guidance add-on code (76940, 77013, or 77022) based on the modality used.

## Covered ICD-10 Diagnoses

| ICD-10 | Description | Stage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C64.1 | Malignant neoplasm of right kidney, except renal pelvis | T1a–T2 |
| C64.2 | Malignant neoplasm of left kidney, except renal pelvis | T1a–T2 |
| C64.9 | Malignant neoplasm of unspecified kidney | T1a–T2 |
| D30.01 | Benign neoplasm of right kidney | Oncocytoma/AML |
| D30.02 | Benign neoplasm of left kidney | Oncocytoma/AML |
| D41.01 | Neoplasm of uncertain behavior of right kidney | Indeterminate |
| D41.02 | Neoplasm of uncertain behavior of left kidney | Indeterminate |
| Z85.528 | Personal history of other malignant neoplasm of kidney | Surveillance/re-ablation |
| Q61.3 | Polycystic kidney, unspecified (VHL-related) | Hereditary syndrome |
| D36.7 | Benign neoplasm of other specified sites (VHL/TSC) | Hereditary syndrome |

## Payer-Specific Requirements

### CMS / Medicare (LCD L35041)

**Covered Indications:**
- T1a renal cell carcinoma (≤4 cm) confirmed by biopsy or strongly suspected on imaging in patients who are poor surgical candidates
- T1b RCC (4–7 cm) in patients with high surgical risk, solitary kidney, or hereditary RCC syndromes
- Benign renal tumors (oncocytoma, AML) when symptomatic, enlarging, or at risk for hemorrhage
- Re-ablation for local recurrence or incomplete treatment after prior ablation

**Non-Covered:**
- T2 or higher renal masses as primary treatment
- Metastatic disease (ablation of primary in setting of known metastases requires individual review)
- Simple renal cysts (Bosnak I/II) without malignant features

**Documentation Requirements:**
- Cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) with tumor size, location, and R.E.N.A.L. score
- Biopsy result or documentation of why biopsy was deferred
- Surgical risk assessment (anesthesia consult or surgeon note for high-risk designation)
- Renal function (eGFR) and contralateral kidney status

### BlueCross BlueShield

- Covered for T1a RCC in patients who are poor surgical candidates or who decline surgery after informed consent
- T1b: covered for high surgical risk patients, solitary kidney, hereditary syndromes, or bilateral tumors
- Pre-ablation biopsy required or documented rationale for proceeding without biopsy
- Prior authorization required; submit CT/MRI images, biopsy report, and surgical risk documentation
- BCBS Medical Policy: Ablation of Renal Tumors (updated 2023)

### Aetna

- Covered for T1a RCC (≤4 cm) in high surgical risk patients or those with solitary/poorly functioning contralateral kidney
- T1b: covered when partial nephrectomy is not technically feasible or patient is high surgical risk
- Hereditary RCC syndromes: covered regardless of tumor size when nephron-sparing approach is indicated
- Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin #0649: Ablation Therapies for Renal Cell Carcinoma (updated 2023)
- Requires: CT or MRI with tumor size and location, biopsy or imaging-based diagnosis, eGFR, surgical risk assessment

### Cigna

- Covered for T1a RCC in patients who are not surgical candidates or who prefer ablation after informed discussion of comparative outcomes
- T1b: covered for high surgical risk, solitary kidney, hereditary syndromes, or bilateral synchronous tumors
- Cigna Coverage Policy: Ablation of Renal Tumors (2024)
- Pre-ablation biopsy strongly preferred; document rationale if not performed
- R.E.N.A.L. nephrometry score should be documented in the procedure planning note

### UnitedHealthcare

- Covered for T1a RCC (≤4 cm) confirmed by biopsy in patients who are poor surgical candidates
- T1b: covered for high surgical risk patients with documented anesthesia or surgical consultation
- UHC Medical Policy: Ablation of Renal Tumors (updated 2024)
- Biopsy required prior to ablation unless documented contraindication to biopsy
- Submit: imaging report with R.E.N.A.L. score, biopsy pathology, eGFR, surgical risk documentation
- Peer-to-peer review available and recommended for T1b cases in surgically fit patients
